subject: Control plane maintenance: KV-cache warm-up + rolling restarts (us-east-1)
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Platform Ops <platformops@acme-pay.com>, Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme-pay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Control plane maintenance: KV-cache warm-up + rolling restarts (us-east-1)

Hi Tim / Platform Ops team,

We wanted to give you an advance notice of a planned control-plane maintenance window that may cause brief client-visible effects for workloads in us-east-1.

Schedule
- Start: 2026-07-09 02:00 UTC
- End:   2026-07-09 04:00 UTC
- Duration: ~2 hours (staged, rolling across availability zones)

What we're doing
- In-place kernel/driver refresh for control-plane nodes.
- A KV-cache warm-up phase after each restart to preserve inference cold-start characteristics.
- Rolling restarts to avoid long single-node outages.

Expected user impact
- Majority of requests: no action required; minor latency bump (most <500ms) during warm-up.
- Small fraction of requests may see transient 503s or connection resets while a node drains (~30-90s per node during rotation).
- Streaming sessions may experience brief interruptions; clients should reconnect/continue where supported.

Mitigations
- We will route in-flight traffic to healthy replicas and use routing fallbacks to reduce impact.
- Automatic KV-cache prewarming for pinned deployments where possible.
- We will run a canary sequence before broad rollout and monitor health and SLOs closely.

Action for you
- No required action for most customers. If you rely on long-lived streaming sessions or have strict windowing requirements, please reply with a preferred shorter blackout window or ask for a canary in us-west-2.
- If you prefer us to orchestrate a cross-region failover for the maintenance window, let us know and we will coordinate the steps and timing.

Attachments: control_plane_maintenance_runbook.pdf (runbook), kv-cache-warmup-diagram.png (illustration)
Related status: https://status.redwood.com/incident/20260709-cp-maintenance

I'll send a follow-up with the canary results ~24h before the window.

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.com

From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme-pay.com>

Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane maintenance: KV-cache warm-up + rolling restarts (us-east-1)

Thanks Ethan — appreciate the heads up.

A couple quick questions:
1) Our payout pipeline uses streaming responses and keeps connections open for up to 6 minutes. Can you confirm what "brief interruptions" typically mean for streams? Is automatic reconnection guaranteed or will we need to handle replays?
2) If we request a canary in us-west-2, can you guarantee no data plane change (we must avoid any model version change during the window)?
3) If the maintenance causes an SLA breach, what is the process for a credit request?

We'd like a canary if possible — preferred window is the same night but shifted +2 hours. Please advise.

—Tim
Tim Lee
SRE Lead, Acme Payments
tim.lee@acme-pay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme-pay.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane maintenance: KV-cache warm-up + rolling restarts (us-east-1)

Thanks, Tim — looping in Ops and CS details.

Quick answers:
- Streaming: interruptions are typically connection drops at the point of socket rebind; our client SDK will attempt a quick reconnect, but application-level replay is not automatic. We'll add a short sticky retry policy on the edge to help with streaming resumption. For Acme's 6m streams, we'll coordinate a prewarm to reduce likelihood of mid-stream resets.
- Canaries/Model versions: we will not change model versions for canaries unless you explicitly request an upgrade. The canary will run same model variant and same quantization profile.
- SLA credit: standard credit process applies — please open a ticket referencing incident id CP-MAINT-20260709 and we'll run the postmortem; support will attach metrics and token-level billing delta for the window.

Action items assigned:
- @Grace O'Connor: prepare a us-west-2 canary plan (duration: 30m) and brief checklist for Acme by EOD 2026-07-07.
- @Rachel Kim: prepare the routing/fallback update and confirm that pinned deployments for Acme won't be repointed unless they approve.
- @Ethan Park: confirm the +2h shifted window option for the canary and send final canary invite to Tim.

I'll update the runbook with the answers and link to the canary playbook. Attaching a quick ops checklist.
